panel.loginHint: Sign in to manage the Xray core.
panel.hintMissing: No core found on this server. It installs with the official XTLS script, keeping standard paths and service.
panel.hintOk: Updating only swaps the binary; your config is untouched.
panel.name: Name (email)
panel.confirmDelInbound: Delete this inbound and all its clients?
panel.confirmApi: This adds an API inbound on 127.0.0.1 and its routing rule to the config. Continue?
panel.confirmRestore: Replace the current config with this backup? (the current one is backed up too)
panel.publicHost: Server domain or IP for links
panel.sslHint: Panel and subscription SSL are set in the SSH menu: run xray-one, option 4.
panel.qBackups: Before every change the previous Xray config is saved here (last 40). Restore tests it first and only brings back the Xray config; panel users and settings are not touched.
panel.qRaw: The current Xray config file as it is on the server; view only, edit through this panel.
panel.quickHint: Every type you tick gets its own free port and one shared client, so that client's subscription carries them all.
panel.gPlain: No TLS (for relays or CDN over HTTP)
panel.needCert: Set SSL in the SSH menu first
panel.relayHint: Every client gets an extra link with this address (also in QR and subscription). SNI, keys and other settings stay the same. The panel does not build the route; this address must already reach this server.
panel.relayEx: Examples: a second subdomain pointing to this IP (if the first gets blocked) · a Cloudflare subdomain or clean IP for WS/XHTTP+TLS inbounds · the IP of a server you forward here yourself with iptables/HAProxy.
panel.relayNoClient: This inbound has no client yet to preview a link.
panel.editIbNote: Protocol, tag and clients stay. Changing the port or settings changes links and the subscription; users must update their sub.
panel.rsHint: Checks from this server which sites work as a REALITY target (TLS 1.3, h2, X25519, valid certificate). Leave empty for common sites, or enter a domain, an IP or a range like 1.2.3.0/24.
panel.rsPh: domain, IP or range — empty = common sites
panel.tbHint: Selected inbounds open on the middle server on their own port. Ports busy there are skipped and shown here.
panel.tbProgress: {a} of {b} ready on the middle server
panel.tbSlow: The middle server did not answer. Check it is online in the Tunnels tab.
panel.stUnknown: old agent; rerun the install command
panel.confirmDelSel: Delete {n} selected inbounds? Their clients go too.
panel.usersHint: A client is one name that sits on several inbounds, with one traffic/time limit and one subscription link for all of them.
panel.confirmDelUser: Remove this client from every inbound?
panel.tnHost: Middle server IP or domain (for SSH)
panel.mRealityD: No domain or cert needed; looks like a visit to a real site.
panel.tpHint: Each port is checked as free (TCP and UDP) before saving. If a server is connected with that method, switch its method first, then change the port.
panel.mXhttpD: HTTP/2 + TLS, looks like normal HTTPS; WS successor.
panel.mBackhaulD: This server dials the middle server with Backhaul; VLESS inside.
panel.mAsk: Switch this middle server to "{m}"? If it can't connect within 90 s it goes back by itself.
panel.mBack: The new method did not connect and went back: {x}
panel.mNeedAgent: To switch methods, run the install command on the middle server once more (version {v} or newer).
panel.tnPassKey: Panel key installed; no password needed
panel.tnQuick: Quick install without a password: run this on the middle server as root. Valid 24 h, void after it connects.
panel.qSingle: This inbound (SOCKS or HTTP) has no client list, just one username and password, so everyone uses this one link. Link form: http://user:pass@server:port (for SOCKS, user:pass is base64). Works in any app with a proxy setting, or v2rayN/NekoBox. Not encrypted.
panel.qDomain: Optional. If the middle server cannot reach this server, this server dials the middle server itself (reverse path). Without a domain only REALITY is tried; with a domain and SSL, WS and XHTTP too. Not used in user links.
panel.qRtT: The site the REALITY tunnel looks like a visit to, on this server and, on the reverse path, on the middle server. It can differ from your inbounds' sites. Needs TLS 1.3, h2 and X25519: Check tests it from this server and the middle servers.
panel.mGreD: A GRE link between the two servers' IPs (protocol 47) with VLESS inside. Light and fast; no encryption of its own, and no NAT.
panel.mFrpD: This server dials the middle server with FRP (like the reverse path); VLESS inside.
panel.mSshD: Built-in SSH tunnel; on the wire it is just an SSH connection. No extra program.
panel.qFrag: The first TLS message goes out in small pieces; some filters only block when they see the site name in one whole packet. One switch for WS and XHTTP on every middle server.
panel.cOverGreHint: This server dials the middle server inside the GRE link (GRE must work between the servers).
panel.mNoGre: Not ready: GRE needs both servers' public IPs
panel.mNoSshKey: Waiting for the middle server's SSH key…
panel.qCPort: This port opens on the middle servers and this server dials it; open it in their firewall if they have one (UDP for kcp and quic).
panel.qGre: GRE is protocol 47, not TCP or UDP; if a firewall or the datacenter blocks it, rotation moves on to the next method.
panel.mWgD: Over UDP, straight to this server's IP. If UDP is blocked between the servers, rotation moves on to the next method.
panel.mKcpD: VLESS over mKCP (UDP), encrypted; steadier on lossy links, but uses more traffic.
panel.poolHint: Untick to keep the middle server from searching or rotating to this method. The active method is always in.
panel.mNoUdp: Not ready: set the UDP address
panel.mNoKcp: Not ready: this server needs Xray {v} or newer
panel.mOldMid: Update the middle server (run the install command again)
panel.udpHint: Middle servers connect to this address over UDP: a direct IP, not a domain behind a CDN.
panel.tnInfo: The middle server connects to {domain}; pick each server's method on its cards (WS on port {port}{x}). User → middle server → this server → internet.
panel.tnNeedSSL: The WSS tunnel needs this server's domain and SSL: set them in the SSH menu first.
panel.tnPick: Which middle servers should this inbound use? Each one gets its own link.
panel.tnTestBad: No answer from the middle server
panel.rvVia: Direct path on fallback method {m} (found by searching)
panel.rvSearch: Main is searching for the middle server: way {m}
panel.rvCool: Every way tried; resting until {t}, then starting over
panel.rvOld: For two-way reconnect and a domain, run the install command on the middle server once more (version {v} or newer).
panel.dmHint: Add an A record to {ip} (gray cloud in Cloudflare), then save. The middle server gets SSL itself; its port 80 must be free.
panel.tnRemove: Remove the relay from the middle server (run there):
panel.tnDeploying: Installing on the middle server… (a few minutes)
panel.tnConfirmDel: Remove this middle server? Inbounds stop using it.
panel.wgHint: For the official WireGuard app: download the file and tap + then Import from file, or scan the QR with Create from QR code.
panel.portsHint: Every inbound port, comma separated, for building relays and tunnels.
panel.gProxy: Plain proxies (SOCKS / HTTP, own user and password)
panel.sniIntro: With no VPN, a user sets their device's DNS to an entry server's IP. Only the listed domains go through the server; the rest of the internet stays direct.
panel.sniS2h: Each ticked server runs the DNS and the 80/443 entry. If the main server is filtered in Iran, pick a middle server.
panel.sniS3h: Addresses that pressed Activate on a subscription page. Removing one stops it until it activates again.
panel.sniS4h: Names active devices asked the DNS for. If a game fails, add the new names that showed up while you opened it.
panel.sniOnlyNew: Only names not in the list
panel.sniAddAll: The whole domain with all its subdomains
panel.sniAddOne: Only this name and its subdomains
panel.sniSeenOld: To see this server's addresses and names, its agent must be {v}.
panel.sniNeedDom: Save the domains in part 1 first.
panel.qSni: For games and sites that refuse Iranian addresses, with no VPN. A user sets their phone's or console's DNS to an entry server's IP; only the domains in this list pass through that server, the rest of the internet stays direct. Only addresses of users who pressed Activate on their subscription page can use it. Ports 53, 80 and 443 must be free on that server. It does not get around filtering and the site name is visible.
panel.sniDoms: Domains (one per line; subdomains are included)
panel.sniMain: The main server is an entry too
panel.sniHint: Ready lists are a starting point and need a test with the real game; add missing names from part 4.
panel.sniNoDom: Enter the domains in the Game unblocker box at the top first.
panel.sniOld: This server's agent must be {v} or newer: run a new install command on it.
panel.sniNoIP: This server's public IP is not known yet.
panel.dtHint: A fixed path, separate from the rotating tunnel: it never switches and has no fallback. Inbounds pinned to it go only this way, and stay down if it drops.
panel.dtWgD: Xray WireGuard over UDP; the middle server dials this server's IP directly. Won't work if UDP is blocked between the servers.
panel.dtKcpD: Xray VLESS over mKCP (UDP), tuned for gaming and encrypted with a seed; the middle server dials this server's IP directly. Steadier on lossy links, but uses more traffic.
panel.dtAskOnKcp: Turn on dedicated mKCP for this middle server? UDP port {p} on this server must be reachable from it (open it in the firewall).
panel.peAskKcp: Middle servers with the mKCP tunnel reconnect on the new port {p} (a few seconds of drop for inbounds pinned to it). Continue?
panel.spTitle: Ping and speed through this exact path between this server and the middle server (about 48 MB of traffic at most)
panel.spUpd: To test, update the middle server's agent (version {v})
panel.spBusy: Another test is running on this server
panel.dtNeedAgent: Dedicated tunnels need agent {v} or newer: run the install command on the middle server once more.
panel.dtAskOn: Turn on dedicated WireGuard for this middle server? UDP port {p} on this server must be reachable from it.
panel.dtAskOff: Turn off "{t}"? {n} inbounds pinned to it go back to the rotating tunnel.
panel.dtSetHint: Middle servers dial this address and these ports over UDP. Use the direct IP, not a domain behind a CDN. The port must be free (TCP and UDP).
panel.tpBadNum: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535
panel.peAskUsed: Middle servers on "{m}" move to the new port {p}. The old port stays open for 30 minutes so the tunnel does not drop; users may see a few seconds of reconnect. Continue?
panel.peAskWg: Middle servers with the WireGuard tunnel reconnect on the new port {p} (a few seconds of drop for inbounds pinned to it). Continue?
panel.peMoved: Port changed. Middle servers move to it within a minute; the old port stays open for 30 minutes.
panel.dtPickHint: A dedicated path is fixed with no fallback: if it drops, this inbound stays down on that server.
panel.qXu: Checks GitHub for a new Xray once a day. It updates only when you press the button: the current config is tested with the new version first, and a failed test only warns.
panel.xuMid: Middle servers on an older version
panel.xuMidHint: To update them, run the middle server install command on that server again.
panel.qRevPorts: These ports open on the middle server and this server dials them on the reverse path. By default they match this server's tunnel ports (when free on the middle server).
panel.qStart: Only for the first connection. Once the middle server is connected, the other methods join the rotation too. If WS, XHTTP and REALITY are blocked, pick WireGuard or mKCP (over UDP) or GRE. FRP, Backhaul and SSH join after it connects.
panel.qPubIP: GRE links two public IPs directly, so the middle server's IP is needed from the start. If the SSH field holds an IP, that one is used.
sub.title: Subscription
sub.subHint: Add this link to your app so every config updates by itself.
sub.wgHint: Import the file into the official WireGuard app, or scan the QR.
sub.sniHint: For games and sites that refuse Iranian addresses, with no VPN. Turn the VPN off, press Activate, then set your phone's or console's DNS to this address. Activate again whenever your internet changes.
act.okMsg: This internet connection is active for {h} hours. Set your phone's or console's DNS to this address:
act.okHint: Open this link again whenever your internet or SIM card changes, or when the time runs out.
act.badMsg: This activation link is not valid, or your subscription is not active.
panel.confirmDelFolder: Delete this folder? What is inside stays, without a folder.
